note: This pack is neutral Latin American Spanish: tú for one friend, ustedes for a group (never vosotros, which is Spain only). The h in hola is silent — it's just OH-lah.
Estar, not ser: you're asking how someone is right now, not what they are.
y = and, said like a plain "ee".
Plural for no reason anyone can explain — just "good days".
Works as both hello and goodbye once it's dark.
Literally "I call myself". The ll is a plain y sound across most of Latin America.
Said with a handshake (or a kiss on the cheek) the first time you meet.
In Latin America the c is an s: GRAH-syahs. You'll hear GRAH-thyahs in Spain.
v and b are the same sound in Spanish — fah-BOHR, not fah-VOHR.
For bumping into someone or getting past them. Con permiso is "excuse me, coming through".
Sí with an accent is "yes"; si without one is "if".
No "do" in Spanish negatives — just put no in front of the verb.
No "do", no word for "you": the -s ending says who, and your rising voice makes it a question.

natural: I speak a bit of Spanish.
note: Spanish → español: an English s + consonant gets an e in front. And ñ = ny, as in canyon.
Your first engine: quiero + any plain verb. Think "comestibles" for comer.
Fine with friends or at a counter. Quisiera ("I would like") is the softer version.
hoy = today: the h is silent, so it sounds just like English "oy".
You "have" hunger in Spanish — so there's no -o/-a ending to worry about. Same words whoever's speaking.
A man says cansado, a woman cansada — the word follows the speaker. Tired is a state, so estoy.
-o for a man, -a for a woman, on almost every word you use to describe yourself.
Where you're from is part of what you are — so soy, not estoy.
No "a" before a job. Estudiante ends in -e, so it's the same for men and women.
Location always takes estar, even for things that never move.
Two Latin American sounds in one word: z = s, v = b.
tengo que + verb = I have to. Irme is "to take myself off".
Also what you shout at the TV when your team is attacking.
qu = k. The u is just there to keep the c hard.
The everyday goodbye between friends. Adiós can sound a bit final.
mañana = tomorrow, and also morning.
Careful: estoy listo = I'm ready, but soy listo = I'm clever. The verb changes the meaning.
And soy lista = I'm clever. Ser for what you are, estar for how you are right now.
Height is part of what you are, so soy.
Spanish turns liking around: the thing pleases you. Think "gusto".

natural: I don't like it at all.
note: Double negatives are correct Spanish: no … nada.
él (he) has an accent; el (the) doesn't.
hermano / hermana: the same -o/-a switch, on people.
rico = tasty when it's food. A starting r is rolled, like rr.

natural: I'm really happy. (said by a man)
I'm really happy. (said by a woman)

note: Swap to soy aburrido and you've just said "I'm boring".
Think "infirm".
Hours are plural — "they are the three". Only one o'clock is singular: es la una.
voy a + verb = I'm going to — built exactly like English.

natural: I'm going to the beach tomorrow.

note: hacer: silent h, and the c is an s.
The one-word past: comer → comí. It never changes for the speaker's gender.

dialect: Fui al cine con mi novia.
literal: I-went to-the cinema with my girlfriend.
natural: I went to the movies with my girlfriend.
phonetics: FWEE ahl SEE-neh kohn mee NOH-byah.
note: fui = I went (and also I was — ir and ser share their past).

dialect: Fui al teatro con mi novio.
literal: I-went to-the theatre with my boyfriend.
natural: I went to the theater with my boyfriend.
phonetics: FWEE ahl teh-AH-troh kohn mee NOH-byoh.
note: theatre → teatro: Spanish has no th sound, so th is just t.

literal: What you-did the end of week?
natural: What did you do at the weekend?
phonetics: KEH ee-SEES-teh ehl FEEN deh seh-MAH-nah?

note: dormir → dormí. Think "dormitory".
Spanish says "the head", not "my head" — the me already says whose.
Weather is something that "makes" itself: hace calor, hace frío.
Said, and meant, when someone comes over.

natural: His sister (or her sister) lives in Mexico.
note: The su trap: su = his, her, their, or a formal your. Only context tells you whose sister. And the x in México is a throaty h.
necessary → necesario: -ary becomes -ario, and the double s goes single.
Asking with the plain verb is normal between friends — no "can" needed.
For real apologies and bad news. Perdón is for bumping into people.
The standard answer to an apology.
vivir = to live. Think "vivid", "survive".
me encanta = I love it (it enchants me) — for things, not people.
Plural thing, plural verb: gustan. And roll that rr — pero (but) and perro (dog) are different words.
telephone → teléfono: ph is always f. Day to day most people say el celular.
-ble stays -ble — but you say the e: -bleh.

dialect: Normalmente me levanto a las siete.
literal: Normally me I-raise at the seven.
natural: I usually get up at seven.
phonetics: nohr-mahl-MEHN-teh meh leh-BAHN-toh ah lahs SYEH-teh.
note: normally → normalmente: -ly is -mente. And me levanto is literally "I raise myself".

natural: I've got to have a shower.
note: In much of Latin America bañarse covers showering too.
Think "preoccupied".

natural: I'm used to it by now. (said by a man)
note: Think "accustomed".

natural: I'm used to it by now. (said by a woman)

note: "I stayed asleep" — the classic excuse.

natural: I've been learning Spanish for two years.
note: llevar + time + -ndo = have been doing for. And never drop the tilde from años: without it you've said something anatomical.
Latin America uses the simple past where Spain would say ¿ya has comido?

natural: I forgot. / It slipped my mind.
note: The "it wasn't my fault" construction: the thing forgot itself on me.
Same blameless se. Celular is the Latin American phone; Spain says móvil.

natural: If I have time, I'll call you.
note: The present tense happily covers the near future.

natural: Let me know when you get there.
note: cuando + something that hasn't happened yet takes the subjunctive: llegues, not llegas.
After espero que, gusta turns into guste.

natural: I really want to see you.
note: tener ganas de = to feel like, to be dying to.
Can be easygoing or dismissive — it's all in the tone.
Very Mexican and Central American. Elsewhere you'll hear ¿qué hubo? or ¿qué más?

natural: I'm fed up. (said by a man)
note: Add de: estoy harto de esto = I'm sick of this.

natural: I'm fed up. (said by a woman)

note: The word for embarrassed is avergonzado/a. Never say estoy embarazada unless you mean it — that's "I'm pregnant".

natural: I'm so excited. (said by a man)
note: emotion → emoción, and from it emocionado: thrilled, moved.

natural: I'm so excited. (said by a woman)

note: situation → situación. Complicada ends in -a because situación is feminine — every -ción word is.
Two bridges in one: -ity → -idad, and -ble stays -ble.
nervous → nervioso: -ous becomes -oso (with an i slipped in here).
-oso words agree like any other: -osa for a woman.
experience → experiencia, positive → positivo. Positiva here because experiencia is feminine.

natural: We need to book a table.
note: hay que + verb = one has to — no person named at all.
Friendly, not romantic. Me gustas is the one that means you fancy them.
Latin American. In Spain it's te echo de menos.

dialect: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
literal: If it I-had known, not I-would-have come.
natural: If I'd known, I wouldn't have come.
phonetics: see loh oo-BYEH-rah sah-BEE-doh, noh ah-BREE-ah beh-NEE-doh.
note: The full "if I had … I would have" in Spanish. Notice nothing here agrees with the speaker — haber-tenses never do.

dialect: Estoy convencido de que tiene razón.
literal: I-am convinced-masculine of that she/he-has reason.
natural: I'm sure they're right. (said by a man)
phonetics: ehs-TOY kohn-behn-SEE-doh deh keh TYEH-neh rrah-SOHN.
note: tener razón = to be right (to "have reason").

dialect: Estoy convencida de que tiene razón.
literal: I-am convinced-feminine of that she/he-has reason.
natural: I'm sure they're right. (said by a woman)
phonetics: ehs-TOY kohn-behn-SEE-dah deh keh TYEH-neh rrah-SOHN.

natural: I'm really grateful. (said by a man)
I'm really grateful. (said by a woman)

dialect: A mí no me importa lo que digan.
literal: To me not me it-matters that which they-say.
natural: I don't care what people say.
phonetics: ah MEE noh meh eem-POHR-tah loh keh DEE-gahn.
note: digan is the subjunctive: whatever they may say.

natural: I really hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
note: From Arabic, "if God wills" — but everyone uses it, religious or not. Always followed by the subjunctive.

natural: I find it hard to get up early.
note: me cuesta = it costs me (effort): the natural way to say something's hard for you.
Realizar is a false friend: it means to carry out. "To realise" is darse cuenta.

dialect: Por más que lo intento, no me sale.
literal: For more that it I-try, not to-me it-comes-out.
natural: However hard I try, I can't get it right.
phonetics: pohr MAHS keh loh een-TEHN-toh, noh meh SAH-leh.
note: no me sale = it won't come out right for me.

natural: I was just about to call you.

note: The famous false friend. If you're embarrassed, say me da vergüenza — estoy embarazada is a very different announcement.
fantastic → fantástico: -ic gets an -o, and the stress jumps back (that's what the accent tells you).

natural: Honestly, I'm not sold on it.
note: sincerely → sinceramente: sincera + -mente.
callarse = to go quiet. ¡Cállate! = shut up!
más vale = it's better (literally "more it's worth"). Comes up all the time.
hacer caso = to pay attention, to listen. A parent's classic: ¡hazme caso!

dialect: Me hubiera encantado ir, pero no pude.
literal: To-me it-would-have enchanted to-go, but not I-could.
natural: I'd have loved to go, but I couldn't.
phonetics: meh oo-BYEH-rah ehn-kahn-TAH-doh EER, PEH-roh noh POO-deh.

natural: I was completely wiped out. (said by a man)
note: agotado is also what a shop says when something's sold out.

natural: I was completely wiped out. (said by a woman)

dialect: No es que no quiera, es que no puedo.
literal: Not it-is that not I-want, it-is that not I-can.
natural: It's not that I don't want to — I just can't.
phonetics: noh ehs keh noh KYEH-rah, ehs keh noh PWEH-doh.
note: no es que always pulls the next verb into the subjunctive: quiera.

dialect: Por lo visto, se van a mudar.
literal: By the seen, themselves they-go to to-move.
phonetics: pohr loh BEES-toh, seh bahn ah moo-DAHR.
note: mudarse = to move house. Moverse is just to move your body.

natural: It drives me up the wall.
note: Taken off your hinges, like a door.

natural: I'm dead on my feet. (said by a man)
note: muerto de + a feeling = dying of: muerto de hambre, muerto de risa.

natural: I'm dead on my feet. (said by a woman)
note: Muerta de risa = dying of laughter.

dialect: A estas alturas, ya da lo mismo.
literal: At these heights, already it-gives the same.
natural: At this point, it makes no difference.
phonetics: ah EHS-tahs ahl-TOO-rahs, yah dah loh MEES-moh.

dialect: Me arrepiento de no haberlo dicho antes.
literal: Me I-regret of not to-have-it said before.
natural: I regret not saying it sooner.
phonetics: meh ah-rreh-PYEHN-toh deh noh ah-BEHR-loh DEE-choh AHN-tehs.
note: arrepentirse de = to regret. Same family as "repent".
Literally "may it not even occur to you".

dialect: Más vale que te lo tomes con calma.
literal: More it-is-worth that you it take with calm.
phonetics: MAHS BAH-leh keh teh loh TOH-mehs kohn KAHL-mah.

dialect: Es evidente que algo no cuadra.
literal: It-is evident that something not it-squares.
phonetics: ehs eh-bee-DEHN-teh keh AHL-goh noh KWAH-drah.
note: evident → evidente. cuadrar = to square, to add up — think of a ledger that won't balance.

natural: I was the one who got it wrong.
note: No agreement to worry about — equivocarse works for anyone.

natural: It's my turn to organise the party.
note: me toca = it's my turn. organise → organizar: -ize is -izar.
Short for no me queda otra opción.

dialect: De haberlo sabido, me habría quedado callado.
literal: Of to-have-it known, me I-would-have stayed silent-masculine.
natural: Had I known, I'd have kept my mouth shut. (said by a man)
phonetics: deh ah-BEHR-loh sah-BEE-doh, meh ah-BREE-ah keh-DAH-doh kah-YAH-doh.
note: de + haber + participle is a compact "if I had".

dialect: De haberlo sabido, me habría quedado callada.
literal: Of to-have-it known, me I-would-have stayed silent-feminine.
natural: Had I known, I'd have kept my mouth shut. (said by a woman)
phonetics: deh ah-BEHR-loh sah-BEE-doh, meh ah-BREE-ah keh-DAH-doh kah-YAH-dah.
note: quedado never changes; callada follows the speaker.

dialect: Hay que hacer de tripas corazón.
literal: There-is that to-make of guts heart.
natural: You've just got to grit your teeth and do it.
phonetics: EYE keh ah-SEHR deh TREE-pahs koh-rah-SOHN.
note: Make a heart out of your guts: find courage you don't feel.

dialect: No hay mal que por bien no venga.
literal: Not there-is bad that for good not it-comes.
natural: Every cloud has a silver lining.
phonetics: noh EYE MAHL keh pohr BYEHN noh BEHN-gah.

note: Turned to stone — and since it's de piedra, it's the same for anyone.

dialect: Por mucho que me lo jures, no me lo creo.
literal: For much that to-me it you-swear, not me it I-believe.
natural: However much you swear it, I'm not buying it.
phonetics: pohr MOO-choh keh meh loh HOO-rehs, noh meh loh KREH-oh.
note: jurar = to swear (think "jury"); the j is a throaty h.

dialect: Se me hace agua la boca.
literal: Itself to-me makes water the mouth.
phonetics: seh meh AH-seh AH-gwah lah BOH-kah.

note: Cool and cutting — stronger than me da igual.

natural: I've had it up to here.
note: coronilla = the crown of your head: full to the top. Same for anyone.

natural: Don't bite off more than you can chew.
I never got to do it (and I really wanted to).
note: Left holding the wanting — the feeling of a missed chance.

natural: I'm over the moon. (said by a man)
I'm over the moon. (said by a woman)
note: Encantado/encantada alone is also a warm "pleased to meet you".
